findings.claim: Complete B durable Attempt is persisted before a write, exact repetition only reconciles, conflict/corrupt markers refuse writing and any post-marker uncertain result reconciles without another write; the native tests preserve truthful distinction between real fixture identities and production user approval.
findings.evidence: Source services/aos-api/aos_api/aip_network_issuer_attempt.py SHA256 5a281eaffff81f61a4fd0c5e6ee9c176b62b67230bbb7b6eda226764f8c29603: _reserve_attempt_receipt uses O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_EXCL (atomic exclusive create); FileExistsError routes to _read_prior which raises AttemptAlreadyRecorded for exact match, AttemptConflict for mismatch, AttemptUnknown for corrupt schema. In service.py, reserve happens before the store write call; AfterEach exception handler attempts reconcile and returns unresolved status without another execute write. Test test_budget_policy_renewal_service.py: marker write_bytes corrupted JSON triggers status='unresolved' and marker restored; changed request with wrong expected_source_hash triggers status='conflict'; fault matrix commit_then_drop_return injects RenewalStoreUnknown after COMMIT and lost-service correctly recovers observed status with single marker. Fixture signer uses isolated-b-fixture password in own PG namespace with admin NOLOGIN reset; tokens reject wrong aud/exp/subject/org_id before reservation. Note: claim mentions five modes but schema only defines four operations (propose/decide/revoke/consume) plus readonly reconciliation; readonly mode is exercised via SHOW transaction_read_only check in test.
